quest.title: Shaped by Fame
quest.description: Navia seems to be keeping an eye on something in front of Hotel Debord...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x650, Mora x53900, Hero's Wit x6, Mystic Enhancement Ore x12

talks.objective: Go to the entrance of Hotel Debord

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, Navia! Whatcha up to?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Ah...! Shh...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: ...Why the secrecy?
Get lost, Monica! I don't want to see you back here until you're ready to wake up and start doing things properly! Right now, you're a disgrace to my kitchen and to the Hotel Debord name!

dialogues.speaker: Monica
dialogues.text: I... I—It was an accident...
I'm sorry, did you hear me asking for excuses?

dialogues.speaker: Monica
dialogues.text: No, no! I... I'll do better, I promise...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Why is she so aggressive? She won't even listen to what the poor girl has to say! ...Hey, cut her some slack! You gotta at least hear her out...

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Ah... Wait...!
Huh? Who do you think you are, telling me— Wait a sec... Navia?
...Hmph, so you're bringing backup now? Suit yourself. You're still wasting your time.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: *sigh*

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: ...Savanna, is this how you always treat your staff?

dialogues.speaker: Savanna
dialogues.text: "My staff" is right. I'm the one in charge here now — and last time I checked, the Hotel Debord doesn't take orders from the Spina di Rosula.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Of course, how you run your kitchen is none of our business. But when a member of your staff is so overworked he becomes gravely ill, that most definitely IS our business. We're going to stand up for him, whether you like it or not!

dialogues.speaker: Savanna
dialogues.text: Overworked? Huh, I've said it before and I'll say it again: If Firmin can't handle the job, then tough luck. There are plenty of other capable people I can hire instead!

dialogues.speaker: Monica
dialogues.text: But Firmin can do the job, he just—

dialogues.speaker: Savanna
dialogues.text: Monica, back inside, now!

dialogues.speaker: Monica
dialogues.text: Huh? But you said I shouldn't come back until—

dialogues.speaker: Savanna
dialogues.text: ...Just do as you're told! And not another word out of you. Come on, we have work to do.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow... What a horrible person...

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Sorry, looks like I've dragged you into some drama again...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So, who was that?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Her name is Savanna. She's the new head chef at Hotel Debord.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Ever since she took the job, she's been enforcing a brutal work regime, and putting a huge amount of pressure on her staff...

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: One guy was so overworked, he collapsed from illness. He's been bedridden for days, and he can barely even talk properly...

dialogues.speaker: Firmin
dialogues.text: I'm sorry... I'm sorry... It's all my fault... I don't deserve to be a chef...

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: ...At his family's request, the Spina di Rosula is trying to mediate on his behalf. We're not exactly making a ton of progress, as you saw...

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Savanna is adamant that Firmin's exhaustion and illness have nothing to do with her or how she's been running her kitchen. She's refusing to have any kind of meaningful dialogue with us.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Our next thought was to talk to the other chefs at the restaurant, and get a better idea of their working conditions. But with Savanna watching them like a hawk, no one has been willing to open up...

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: And that's why I'm here, doing it the old-fashioned way. Camping out, watching, and waiting for an opportunity.

choices.text: So you were waiting for Savanna to leave...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...Oh, shoot! It all makes sense now... Sorry, Paimon should have thunk before she spoke. Did Paimon ruin everything...?

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: No, not at all, Paimon! Honestly, the way she was laying into Monica, someone had to step in. I'm sure I would have piped up if you hadn't.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: And besides, I don't really think I'm built for espionage...

choices.text: Either way, Savanna's seen you now...

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Yeah... Meaning it's gonna be all the more difficult to get the inside scoop now. Ugh... I might as well head back to the Fleuve Cendre then. We'll need to come up with a whole new game plan.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Um... Paimon will join you! ...'Cause this is kinda all Paimon's fault...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Then I'll join you too.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Guys, it's fine, you don't need to worry about it! That said... if you were planning to visit the Fleuve Cendre anyway, let me take you out for a meal! I'll make sure it's a proper feast!

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: A really famous chef just joined the Spina di Rosula's tavern! Her name is—

response.speaker: Leone
response.text: Um... sorry to interrupt... I just wanted to apologize for the scene you witnessed just now. We shouldn't subject our customers to that.

response.speaker: Leone
response.text: This is a small token from us... It's some candy from Monica — she asked me to make sure it was delivered into your hands.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Monica's the one apologizing? Hmph, clearly Savanna is the one who owes an apology!

response.speaker: Leone
response.text: Uh... our head chef has been a little highly strung lately... Sorry for everything!

choices.text: Paimon... Don't make things more difficult for her.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Alright... Since there's candy, Paimon will drop it — not the candy!

response.speaker: Leone
response.text: Thank you for understanding! We'll make sure to pass your feedback onto Miss Savanna.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: "A little highly strung," huh...

choices.text: Looks like with Savanna in the kitchen...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon doesn't get it. How did someone like her even become head chef?

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Well, according to Firmin's family, she hasn't always been like this... But that's a story for another time. Let's try this candy!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Ah yes, never underestimate Navia's affinity for sweets...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe, Paimon totally gets it! Come on, dig in!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...Huh? Hold on, there's something written on the wrapper...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: "Find... Escoffier..."?

choices.text: ...Even the waiting staff are on edge.
Thank you for the gift.
So you probably won't get another chance.
And then you were going to approach Monica?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...So, who is this "Escoffier" anyway?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: She... Well, for starters, she used to be the head chef at the Hotel Debord, before Savanna.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: She recreated the legendary Gateau Debord and restored the restaurant back to its former glory...

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Safe to say, she's the most renowned head chef in the Hotel Debord's history after the culinary genius Modeste himself.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Gateau Debord? ...That's the super-exclusive cake that they only sell a few slices a day, right? Wow... Why the heck would she let Savanna take her place?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Well, apparently... The Hotel Debord was reported for a safety incident. Someone claimed that the kitchen was adding an illegal substance to their menu.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: But none of the chefs had any idea how it could have gotten into the food... In the end, Escoffier decided that as head chef, she should take responsibility, and she was sent to the Fortress of Meropide.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The Fortress of Meropide!?

choices.text: Oh, don't be so dramatic. It was probably just a formality...

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Haha... Well, you're right — the quantity of the substance they found was fairly minimal. Even the Gardes believed the whole thing was probably just an accident.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Escoffier didn't have to stay in the Fortress for long, but still, by the time she returned, the role of head chef had already passed to Savanna.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So that's what happened... Paimon still thinks it's really unfair!

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Even though Escoffier is no longer head chef at the Hotel, she's still well respected by the staff.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: So I'm guessing what Monica wants is for us to convince Escoffier to try and negotiate with Savanna on the staff's behalf.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh! Paimon gets it! Monica wants Escoffier to come back and kick Savanna out!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It's simple. If the new head chef is stressing everyone out, then the solution is... just get the old one back!

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Um... Well, about that...
You thought cream of mushroom soup was ready to serve after three and a half minutes on the stove!?
You'd have had more sense serving hot water with ice cubes!
At least then, you wouldn't have wasted all this perfectly good cream and mushroom! What do you say, Hilaire!?

response.speaker: Hilaire
response.text: *sobbing* I'm sorry, cream... I'm sorry, mushroom...

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: As you can see... Escoffier is that kind of chef as well.

choices.text: ...How has the Hotel Debord made it this far?

response.speaker: Escoffier
response.text: ...You have to leave it on the heat for long enough to allow those flavors the chance to come out! Don't be fooled by the aroma when the water first starts to boil. Got it?

response.speaker: Hilaire
response.text: Yes, Chef...

response.speaker: Escoffier
response.text: Then go back and do it again! The customers are still waiting... Remember where you went wrong, and don't repeat the same mistake twice!

response.speaker: Hilaire
response.text: ...Y—Yes, Chef...!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Um... Excuse us, we're—

response.speaker: Escoffier
response.text: Waiting to be served? Sorry, we're pretty busy. I'm afraid you have to join the line...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, no no, we're not here to eat!

response.speaker: Escoffier
response.text: So you're not paying customers? Then I'm afraid the wait will be even longer!

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Haha... It's hard to talk to Escoffier when she's in the zone. Let's take a seat — we can catch up while we wait.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Looks like the rush hour's finally over... Is it always this busy here?

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: These days, yes... I'd say business has tripled since Escoffier joined as temporary head chef.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: She didn't want to go back to Hotel Debord?

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Well, in her words... the Hotel Debord "doesn't need her anymore." It doesn't look like she's got any plans to go back...

response.speaker: Hilaire
response.text: Um... I guess I'll be heading off, then...

response.speaker: Escoffier
response.text: Wait! Take these home with you. We can't serve them now, and there's no sense in letting them go to waste.

response.speaker: Hilaire
response.text: Oh... Thank you, Chef!

response.speaker: Escoffier
response.text: For what? Like I said, I just don't want them going to waste! Oh, and tell Firmin to get well soon, so you're not running yourself ragged every single shift!

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Heh...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: "Firmin"... That's the second time we've heard that name. Who is that, again?

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: ...He's the chef that fell ill from stress. Hilaire is his son, and with mom stuck at home taking care of dad...

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: ...He decided to pick up some work to help pay the bills. Escoffier knows their situation, so she's been making some extra food every day for him to take home...

response.speaker: Escoffier
response.text: Hey! I heard that, Navia!

response.speaker: Escoffier
response.text: I've told you before, no one's making "extra food." Hilaire is making blunders in the kitchen, and I can't serve his failed dishes, so he might as well take them home...

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Yeah, yeah, "failed dishes" that just so happen to be nutritionally complete every single time.

response.speaker: Escoffier
response.text: #Ahem... So, you two must be the world-famous {NICKNAME} and {M#his}{F#her} companion, Paimon, yes? Is there something I can help you with?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, so you know us already! We'll skip the introduction then. We are here to talk about Savanna!

choices.text: Since Hilaire is working for you...

response.speaker: Escoffier
response.text: ...I certainly am. The Spina's headquarters are right next to the tavern, and I've lost count of the number of times Navia's come to pester me about it.

response.speaker: Escoffier
response.text: But... I don't work for the Hotel Debord anymore, and being ex-head chef doesn't give me the right to interfere with their business.

response.speaker: Escoffier
response.text: Besides... I'm the one who persuaded Savanna to take the job in the first place.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What!?

response.speaker: Escoffier
response.text: Well... She was a much gentler person back then. A little timid, even... She wasn't at all confident that she was the right fit for the role.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's hard to believe... Are we definitely talking about the same Savanna here?

response.speaker: Escoffier
response.text: Honestly... I do wonder if she's just emulating me. I mean, I'm not the most pleasant head chef to be around either...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (...At least she's self-aware...)

response.speaker: Escoffier
response.text: Anyway, suffice to say that given the history between us, it'll be tricky for me to tell her she's doing her job wrong without coming across like a huge hypocrite...

response.speaker: Escoffier
response.text: Firmin and the others probably think that Savanna gets it all from me...

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: I wouldn't be so sure about that, Escoffier... Look at this note we got from Monica.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: You give Monica's candy wrapper to Escoffier...

response.speaker: Escoffier
response.text: She mentioned me...

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Whatever shortcomings you feel you have, it looks like Monica still trusts you. As for the others, well... how can you know what they think, unless you ask them?

response.speaker: Escoffier
response.text: Monica...

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Plus, it's not like we're asking you to storm in there and raise hell. We're only in the initial phase of our investigation. All we're trying to do is get the other chefs to open up to us.

response.speaker: Escoffier
response.text: Oh, Monica... Oh, Monica...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...Uh, Escoffier?

response.speaker: Escoffier
response.text: I can't believe her! Powdered sugar is supposed to be applied sparingly! Look at all that on the wrapper — it's thicker than the sole of my shoe!

response.speaker: Escoffier
response.text: Unbelievable! I won't stand for this, she has to learn! Come on, we're going!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait... So now she's...

choices.text: Well, whatever the reason she came up with...

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Heh. Let's go catch up to her. We don't wanna keep her waiting!

choices.text: At least she's convinced herself to go have a conversation.
You must be aware of the situation with Savanna.
I am at a loss for words.
We got sent there just for eating someone else's cake.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: After confirming that this was indeed your attempt at cooking food meant for human consumption, Escoffier looks a little disappointed.

dialogues.speaker: Escoffier
dialogues.text: Huh... I know this doesn't represent what you're capable of. Try again, and this time I want to see you make a proper attempt.

dialogues.speaker: Renaud
dialogues.text: I can't believe I got to witness that firsthand! I only stopped by here for a quick meal... Hehe, I definitely got my Mora's worth today!

dialogues.speaker: Vaneigem
dialogues.text: Ahem, I do apologize... This whole ordeal reflects rather poorly on us...

choices.text: ...Wait, aren't you the boss?

response.speaker: Vaneigem
response.text: I'm afraid it's not quite that simple... The Hotel Debord runs as more of a partnership, you see. It was founded by two friends, Modeste and Savelli, and it's been that way ever since.

response.speaker: Vaneigem
response.text: So, while I am technically Savanna's boss, it's not really my place to interfere with the business of the kitchen.

response.speaker: Vaneigem
response.text: To be perfectly honest with you, that's part of the reason why I suggested a cooking contest.

response.speaker: Vaneigem
response.text: If Escoffier wins, it would be the perfect opportunity for her to talk some sense into Savanna. Or of course, if she wanted to return, then...

response.speaker: Vaneigem
response.text: But anyway, I'm getting ahead of myself. Whatever the outcome, this contest will hopefully serve as a turning point for us... Please pass on my best wishes to Escoffier.

response.speaker: Vaneigem
response.text: ...I must say, Savanna surprised me with her confidence. Does she really believe she can best Escoffier in the kitchen? I thought she was just blowing off steam, when she first raised the idea to me.

choices.text: Can't you rein Savanna in a little?

dialogues.speaker: Monica
dialogues.text: I'm sorry, I'm so sorry! I messed up your order!

dialogues.speaker: Renaud
dialogues.text: Oh... I wouldn't go that far, heh... Maybe the taste is a little off, but if you hadn't brought it up, I don't think I would have noticed...

dialogues.speaker: Monica
dialogues.text: But, but... please, you have to forgive me, or Chef is gonna... Okay, I know! I'll... kneel before you!

dialogues.speaker: Renaud
dialogues.text: What the heck...?

dialogues.speaker: Escoffier
dialogues.text: Get up, Monica! Can't you see that you're just making your customer feel more awkward?

dialogues.speaker: Monica
dialogues.text: Ah... Escoffier?

dialogues.speaker: Escoffier
dialogues.text: If you want forgiveness, then do what any self-respecting chef would do: Make the dish again — and this time, get it right. You cannot go begging your customers to feel sorry for you!

dialogues.speaker: Monica
dialogues.text: I... *sobs* Savanna said that I'm not allowed back in the kitchen until I've corrected my mistake... But if I can't go back into the kitchen, I can't do the dish over...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's some backwards logic... How can you fix your mistake without being allowed to cook? If this is what Firmin had to put up with, then no wonder he had a breakdown...

dialogues.speaker: Escoffier
dialogues.text: ...We apologize for interrupting your meal, Sir.

dialogues.speaker: Renaud
dialogues.text: Ah, it's fine... With my layman's palate, it's not like I can tell the difference anyway, heh... I was actually quite enjoying my meal until she appeared out of nowhere and started apologizing. Gave me a bit of a fright, to be honest...

dialogues.speaker: Monica
dialogues.text: Oh... Well, it's because Chef Savanna tasted a bit of the leftover soup from my pot, and then threw me out of the kitchen...

dialogues.speaker: Renaud
dialogues.text: Gosh, that's pretty strict... Has she always been that way? I don't recall things being like this when Escoffier was head chef here. I gotta say, you're all looking a little worse for wear these days.

dialogues.speaker: Monica
dialogues.text: ...I mean, Escoffier was strict too. But I think the difference is that her criticism was more constructive, so you knew what you did wrong and how to improve. And...

dialogues.speaker: Monica
dialogues.text: We all knew that it came from a good place. Chef Escoffier was hard on us because she truly wanted us to reach her level.

dialogues.speaker: Monica
dialogues.text: But these days... Whenever we make a mistake, we just get told to "wake up," "get your head in the game"... or just "do it again!"

dialogues.speaker: Monica
dialogues.text: And it's only gotten worse since word got out that Chef Escoffier had started working again in the Fleuve Cendre...

dialogues.speaker: Escoffier
dialogues.text: ...Monica, you don't need to call me "Chef." I'm not the boss here anymore.

dialogues.speaker: Monica
dialogues.text: Yeah, but through no fault of your own! What happened back then... that wasn't on you, and all of us know that.

dialogues.speaker: Monica
dialogues.text: That banquet was a huge event, and so many staff were involved every step of the way... With so many moving parts, there's no way of knowing how that lumiline ended up in the food we served.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: "Lumiline"? What's that?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: A new drug from the Fontaine Research Institute, produced from an extract of the Lumitoile. Apparently it sharpens the senses, so they use it to treat people with impaired responses to stimuli.

dialogues.speaker: Renaud
dialogues.text: Oh, yeah! I've heard about that! They found out you can use it as a flavor enhancer since it stimulates the tastebuds... Makes things pretty addictive!

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: They also found that overuse can have mood-altering effects and even lead to nerve damage... So it quickly ended up on the Gardes list of controlled substances.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Unfortunately, however, some food products containing the additive had already made it to the market by the time the Gardes banned it from the restaurant industry.

dialogues.speaker: Monica
dialogues.text: ...Everyone knows that in all likelihood, someone probably just purchased a batch of contaminated ingredients by mistake...

dialogues.speaker: Monica
dialogues.text: But you took all the blame. We all know why — you just didn't wanna see this turn into a place where tensions are constantly running high, because everyone's suspicious of each other all the time...

dialogues.speaker: Monica
dialogues.text: ...And now look at you... A fry chef in the Fleuve Cendre...

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Uhhh... What are you trying to say? Sure, the Spina's tavern is no Hotel Debord, but c'mon, it's not THAT bad... is it?

dialogues.speaker: Renaud
dialogues.text: Oh, the Fleuve Cendre, you say? Great! That's where I'm dining from now on!

dialogues.speaker: Escoffier
dialogues.text: Ahem! Monica, I'm very happy with my current job... And there's no changing the past. We just have to let bygones be bygones.

dialogues.speaker: Escoffier
dialogues.text: Besides... At the end of the day, I was the head chef. Regardless of whose mistake it was, ultimately the responsibility lay with me.

dialogues.speaker: Monica
dialogues.text: *sigh*... If only Savanna was half the boss you were...
I'm sorry? Do you have a problem with my conduct as head chef?

dialogues.speaker: Monica
dialogues.text: Ah! N—No, Chef!

dialogues.speaker: Savanna
dialogues.text: Hmph, so you do remember who's boss.

dialogues.speaker: Savanna
dialogues.text: Escoffier... I thought you'd left this place for good. What are you doing back here?

dialogues.speaker: Escoffier
dialogues.text: ...What happened to you, Savanna? Why are you acting like this? When I turned this place over to you, I—

dialogues.speaker: Savanna
dialogues.text: You made me the head chef, and gave up your right to tell me how to do my job!

dialogues.speaker: Savanna
dialogues.text: You're not the boss here anymore... So stop acting like you own the place!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa... sounds like someone has a chip on her shoulder...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Maybe we should give them some space...

dialogues.speaker: Escoffier
dialogues.text: SAVANNAAAA!

dialogues.speaker: Escoffier
dialogues.text: My god, have you grown a temper since I last saw you!

dialogues.speaker: Escoffier
dialogues.text: Have you put even half the amount of energy into improving your cooking skills? Or are you still using the Pluie Lotus as an off-brand Marcotte, thinking no one can tell the difference?

dialogues.speaker: Savanna
dialogues.text: Th—That's none of your business!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What happened to not storming in and raising hell...?
Hoho, I was not expecting to see something this spicy as soon as Escoffier returned!

dialogues.speaker: Escoffier
dialogues.text: Huh? Vaneigem?

dialogues.speaker: Vaneigem
dialogues.text: Aye, miladies. Might I make a humble suggestion? Given that we have ourselves a tete-a-tete between chefs at the Hotel Debord... I daresay it would be "de rigueur" to settle this the traditional way.

dialogues.speaker: Renaud
dialogues.text: The traditional way? That can only mean one thing!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Sounds like we're in for a history lesson...

dialogues.speaker: Vaneigem
dialogues.text: That's right! I'm talking, of course, about the tradition established by Modeste himself... The cooking contest!

dialogues.speaker: Renaud
dialogues.text: According to legend, the founders of Hotel Debord, Modeste and Savelli, used this method to resolve all of their disputes! Everything from petty arguments over next week's menu, to disagreements over the strategic direction of the restaurant...

dialogues.speaker: Renaud
dialogues.text: ...The cooking contest would decide who had the final say!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sounds like they had a lot of free time on their hands...

dialogues.speaker: Vaneigem
dialogues.text: Ah, well it might sound that way to us, but in fact the cooking contest played an enormous role in motivating chefs to hone their skills, reaching new heights of excellence in the culinary arts!

dialogues.speaker: Vaneigem
dialogues.text: And indeed, the reintroduction of this institution in recent years has surely been instrumental in transforming the Hotel Debord into the top-ranking restaurant in Fontaine.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Reintroduction? Someone brought it back? Who?

dialogues.speaker: Vaneigem
dialogues.text: What say you, Escoffier? Surely, you of all people won't back down from this challenge? It was you who put the rule in place, after all.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Thought so. There's your answer, Paimon...

dialogues.speaker: Escoffier
dialogues.text: Ahem... Sure, I reinstated it, but I'm not a chef at Hotel Debord anymore. Isn't this bending the rules a little?

dialogues.speaker: Vaneigem
dialogues.text: Haha, I see no issue as long as both sides agree to the terms. We could simply treat it as an... exhibition of sorts. Savanna, any objections?

dialogues.speaker: Savanna
dialogues.text: "Exhibition"? Hmph... No.

dialogues.speaker: Savanna
dialogues.text: If we're going to battle it out, let's put it all on the line! If I lose, it's up to you what happens to me!

dialogues.speaker: Escoffier
dialogues.text: ...I don't want anything to "happen" to you...

dialogues.speaker: Savanna
dialogues.text: But if you lose... you hand over the Codex Debord to me!

dialogues.speaker: Renaud
dialogues.text: What!? THE Codex Debord!?

choices.text: The Codex Debord!? ...Uh...

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: ...Only the legendary handbook written by the original head chef, Modeste! It contains all his secret recipes, including Gateau Debord!

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: It's the greatest treasure in Fontaine's culinary world, and only the present and former head chefs of the Hotel Debord have the right to read it!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Present and former...? Wait, but that already includes Savanna though...

response.speaker: Escoffier
response.text: What do you want that old thing for? You have your own copy, don't you?

response.speaker: Savanna
response.text: Hmph, don't take me for a fool. You know perfectly well what I mean...

response.speaker: Savanna
response.text: I want YOUR copy — the original version. The one you took with you when you left us!

response.speaker: Escoffier
response.text: ...I'm sorry, I must be missing something. You know there's no difference between the original and the copy, right? They contain the exact same recipes...

response.speaker: Savanna
response.text: Stop trying to change the topic. What's wrong, Escoffier? Scared you're gonna lose to me? Or are you scared of me getting my hands on the original Codex?

response.speaker: Vaneigem
response.text: Um, Savanna, you may remember that we gave her the original as a parting gift, to thank Escoffier for her years of service... Asking for it back feels a little... ahem...

response.speaker: Savanna
response.text: Oh, I'm sure it won't be an issue — as long as both sides agree to the terms. Those were your words, weren't they?

response.speaker: Savanna
response.text: And as for the contest itself... Let's make it a bake-off. Gateau Debord, per the recipe in the Codex! Well, Escoffier? You against me — are you in or out?

response.speaker: Escoffier
response.text: Hmph... You sound surprisingly confident.

response.speaker: Escoffier
response.text: ...Alright then. Let's see how much you've actually grown.

response.speaker: Escoffier
response.text: I hope you surprise me, Savanna... I'd hate to find out that all you've learned after this long is how to chew people's heads off!

response.speaker: Savanna
response.text: Hmph... Believe me, I'll show you.

choices.text: ...Um, what is that?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Um, so... This whole bake-off thing kinda came outta nowhere. Was it really sensible to just go along with it?

dialogues.speaker: Escoffier
dialogues.text: Well, I got a sense that she's holding something back. But we chefs always express ourselves in our cooking. So if she won't talk, this might be the best way to find out what's really going on with her.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Holding back? Sure didn't sound that way to Paimon...

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Escoffier only picked up on it because she's the same way... Always closed-off, never letting you know what she really thinks!

dialogues.speaker: Escoffier
dialogues.text: That's patently false — at least where your macarons are concerned. I've been nothing but truthful with you about the disgraceful amount of sugar you use.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: ...Okay, that's one case where you can keep your thoughts to yourself!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So anyway, what's this "Codex Debord" she's so obsessed with?

dialogues.speaker: Escoffier
dialogues.text: Oh, that... Well, it's not so much a recipe book as a diary of Modeste's adventures.

dialogues.speaker: Escoffier
dialogues.text: Back in the day, he and his good friend Savelli explored far and wide, partly adventuring, partly looking for new ingredients and developing new recipes. Their creations had an enormous influence on the course of Fontaine cuisine, turning it into a much more vibrant and diverse scene.

dialogues.speaker: Escoffier
dialogues.text: For instance, legend has it that the original Gateau Debord was made using a special secret ingredient that Modeste discovered on one of his adventures.

dialogues.speaker: Escoffier
dialogues.text: So rare was the ingredient that they could never make more than sixteen slices of the cake per day... But everyone who tried it claimed that it was one of the most blissful and invigorating things they had ever tasted.

dialogues.speaker: Escoffier
dialogues.text: Modeste and Savelli went on to found the original Hotel Debord, which catapulted them to stardom in Fontaine's culinary world.

dialogues.speaker: Escoffier
dialogues.text: Especially Modeste. He was hailed as a once-in-a-generation genius, and over time, the recipes from his adventure log became known as the "Codex Debord."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ah, Paimon's heard this kind of story before... "Armed with the Codex, the Hotel Debord took its rightful place as the finest restaurant in the land, serving those recipes for centuries to come"... Something like that?

dialogues.speaker: Escoffier
dialogues.text: What? No, of course not. Cooking is a constantly evolving art form. How could any restaurant survive if they only served food that was popular last century?

dialogues.speaker: Escoffier
dialogues.text: Anyway, never mind centuries — Savelli and Modeste parted ways not even ten years after their rise to fame. Then, Modeste passed away while he was still in his prime...

dialogues.speaker: Escoffier
dialogues.text: ...And that was it, the end of the Hotel Debord's heyday. It fell into decline, and for most of its history it was just a nondescript place with a couple of cheap tables. It's only in recent decades that it started recovering.

dialogues.speaker: Escoffier
dialogues.text: Even then, it still took numerous relocations and changes of management before we finally ended up with Vaneigem and the restaurant we have today.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh... So the Codex really isn't all that, then. Paimon figured it was like one of those mystical books they have in Liyue's martial arts novels, where the main character learns all their secret powers from.

dialogues.speaker: Escoffier
dialogues.text: Yes, well that's fiction, and this is reality. You can't meet the tastes of modern diners by following some ancient recipes from a dusty old book.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Case in point — even the Gateau Debord they sell now is actually Escoffier's reimagination.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, really? Why though? Didn't that recipe make it into the Codex?

dialogues.speaker: Escoffier
dialogues.text: It did, but like I said — it's a dusty old book now, and the records aren't as legible as they once were. Not to mention that there's no way of finding the secret ingredient Modeste wrote about.

dialogues.speaker: Escoffier
dialogues.text: So, "reimagination" is right. I consulted some historical records and took what I could from the Codex, but ultimately the Gateau Debord of today is my own recipe.

dialogues.speaker: Escoffier
dialogues.text: As for why we gave it the same name, and kept the tradition of only selling sixteen slices a day... Well, you've got Vaneigem's business sense to thank for that.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh... Huh, well that kinda takes all the mystique out of it...

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Hey now, it might not be the original "Gateau Debord," but it's still the most delicious cake in Fontaine today! And who knows — maybe Escoffier's version is more suited to your palate?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Just think, if the original truly was the perfect cake you're imagining it to be, there's no way the recipe would've been lost to history, right? Not to mention that the Hotel Debord never would've fallen into a slump.

dialogues.speaker: Escoffier
dialogues.text: Anyway... Before I left my role as head chef, I made a copy of all the recipes from the Codex, including my own improved versions, and turned them over to Savanna.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh... So why is she so interested in the original copy?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Could it be a symbolic thing? Like, whoever holds the original Codex Debord is the "true" head chef?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Well, it was clearly precious enough to give to Escoffier as a parting gift. Meanwhile, Savanna only got a copy...

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Maybe from her point of view, it's like management doesn't truly see her as being worthy of the role.

dialogues.speaker: Escoffier
dialogues.text: You think so? ...The only thing is, it was her suggestion to gift me the original in the first place. Well, a joint decision by her and Vaneigem, but still...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What!? Huh... Guess she's had a major change of heart since she became head chef... Yeesh...

dialogues.speaker: Escoffier
dialogues.text: ...Who knows, we could speculate forever. Better to just let our gateau do the talking.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What does that mean, exactly?

dialogues.speaker: Escoffier
dialogues.text: It means besting her in this bake-off — and then getting her to explain herself! Even if I have to beat it out of her with a spatula!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You don't mince words...

dialogues.speaker: Escoffier
dialogues.text: However much she's changed since we worked together, I believe that she still has her chef's pride. And if she respects the art, she'll respect the outcome of our contest.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Well, I'm confident that you and your spatula can get justice for Firmin. All you need to do now is win the contest, but that should be a breeze for you!

dialogues.speaker: Escoffier
dialogues.text: Eh, let's not get too ahead of ourselves... Gateau Debord is very complicated to make — usually, it takes three chefs working in tandem to cover everything.

dialogues.speaker: Escoffier
dialogues.text: Now, if I had to push it, I could probably do the work of three chefs myself... But I'd prefer to play it safe if I can find a couple of assistants in time.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, that's easy! The three of us are veterans in the kitchen. You just need to pick two of us!

dialogues.speaker: Escoffier
dialogues.text: #Well, I have heard that {NICKNAME} is an accomplished cook as well as a warrior... But be warned, I will hold you to exceptionally high standards. Think you're up to the task?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Bring it on!

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Count me in, too! I've spent weeks perfecting my macarons after your scathing review!

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: #Even if it means competing against {NICKNAME}, so be it! I'll show you what I'm made of!

dialogues.speaker: Escoffier
dialogues.text: Hmm, confident. I like it. Alright, let's start with some elementary mise en place — show me your knife skills.

dialogues.speaker: Escoffier
dialogues.text: And done! These are the flavor compounds extracted from our ingredients. I've processed all the fruit you chopped up earlier.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Mmm... Wow, even the smell is so much more concentrated! What next? Do we add all this stuff in?

dialogues.speaker: Escoffier
dialogues.text: Absolutely not! Throwing everything in at once will ruin the balance of flavors! We have to go slowly and carefully, to calibrate the exact flavor we want.

dialogues.speaker: Escoffier
dialogues.text: ...I'll demonstrate again. Now, watch closely!

dialogues.speaker: Escoffier
dialogues.text: Hm... Looks like you found that easier than I expected.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, thankfully it was pretty straightforward in the end! You made it sound like we'd be carving statues out of fruits, or something...

dialogues.speaker: Escoffier
dialogues.text: Well brace yourself, because the next step is anything but straightforward. I'll be using this cold press to extract flavor compounds from the ingredients.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What's a cold press?

dialogues.speaker: Escoffier
dialogues.text: A kind of special food processor I got the Fontaine Research Institute to make for me. It uses cold-temperature extraction to isolate the essence of cooking ingredients, which can then be used to flavor dishes more precisely...

dialogues.speaker: Escoffier
dialogues.text: But um... this isn't exactly standard kitchen equipment, so that probably didn't make a whole lot of sense... Let me give you a demonstration instead.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Escoffier's face lights up as you present your finished dish...

dialogues.speaker: Escoffier
dialogues.text: Ahh... Look at that! With the grace of a Snow-Winged Goose, as I like to say! Now, let the grading commence!

talks.objective: Use the cold press to extract flavor compounds

dialogues.speaker: Firmin
dialogues.text: ...So, this is what Chef Escoffier is truly capable of...

talks.objective: Balance the flavors of your dish

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: After closely examining your dish, Escoffier asks you some pointed questions...

dialogues.speaker: Escoffier
dialogues.text: ...Hmm. So what is this, exactly? Because what it looks like is the aftermath of an alchemy accident. You realize food is supposed to be edible, yes?

dialogues.speaker: Escoffier
dialogues.text: And voila! Whew... Now, it's your turn.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: With Escoffier's guidance, everyone completes the flavoring process...

dialogues.speaker: Escoffier
dialogues.text: Hmm... Not terrible. Considering this was everyone's first time blending flavor extracts, it could've been worse.

dialogues.speaker: Escoffier
dialogues.text: #But {NICKNAME}'s work was surprisingly good... Are you sure you've never done this before? You got almost perfect results on your first try...

choices.text: All thanks to my excellent teacher!

response.speaker: Escoffier
response.text: Hmph, that goes without saying! Still, credit where credit's due — you did well.

response.speaker: Escoffier
response.text: Alright, now for the part I've been looking forward to: I want each of you to cook something from the Hotel Debord's current menu. I'll judge your submissions, and give you a final score.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: ...Final score?

response.speaker: Escoffier
response.text: That's right — the true test of your cooking skills is the finished product! It'll be good practice for the contest itself — now get to it. Chop chop!

choices.text: I guess I just treated it like an adventurer's puzzle...

response.speaker: Escoffier
response.text: Huh... Well, they do say adventurers are multitalented folks. Now I've seen it firsthand!

dialogues.speaker: Escoffier
dialogues.text: Alright, if you insist... then prepare for some of the finest food of your lives!

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Escoffier treats everyone to a spectacular feast...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Escoffier opted for a huge variety of dishes... Thankfully, both of us are skilled enough that, even though it was our first time working together, we had a great rapport.)

dialogues.speaker: Escoffier
dialogues.text: Hmm, that's not a bad idea actually... Wait, hold on! You need to finesse that further...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (She dished out plenty of praise, and taught me an awful lot too. The time seemed to fly by.)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hehe... Pretty good, right? Not to brag or anything, but Paimon's a bit of a connoisseur when it comes to le food!

dialogues.speaker: Escoffier
dialogues.text: Hmm... Six points.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What? ...*sigh* Well, fair enough. Paimon doesn't cook all that often, so as long as it's a pass...

dialogues.speaker: Escoffier
dialogues.text: That's six out of a hundred.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: WHAT!?

dialogues.speaker: Escoffier
dialogues.text: You say you're a connoisseur, but it's quite clear from this dish that you have far more experience consuming food than creating it!

dialogues.speaker: Escoffier
dialogues.text: By that logic, I suppose you think listening to Lady Furina on repeat every day would make you an opera singer?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Aw...

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Me next, me next! I'll have you know that this batch of macarons has two whole tablespoons less sugar than my previous ones!

dialogues.speaker: Escoffier
dialogues.text: So you went from twelve tablespoons to ten? Well, it's nice to know you actually measured it out! Because it tastes like you just threw in whatever was left in the jar! Six points.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Yikes, she's a harsh judge...

dialogues.speaker: Escoffier
dialogues.text: Now to the final dish... Hmm...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So, uh... Wh—What do you think...?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: This is our last hope!

dialogues.speaker: Escoffier
dialogues.text: ...Eight points.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Darn... That's barely higher than what we got...

dialogues.speaker: Escoffier
dialogues.text: Not exactly... The color is spot-on, beautiful aroma, excellent presentation...

dialogues.speaker: Escoffier
dialogues.text: ...I have to give this one eight points out of ten! ...Maybe even nine points!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh!? How did you pull that off?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: It's all that practice from cooking for you, Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Escoffier
dialogues.text: Don't get me wrong, there's room for improvement... But still, this is clearly the work of an accomplished chef! I can tell that you've put many hours of work into honing your skills in the kitchen.

dialogues.speaker: Escoffier
dialogues.text: #I can really taste the grace of the Snow-Winged Goose in this dish! {NICKNAME}'s journey, with all its trials, tribulations, and setbacks... not to mention the frustrations of having a picky eater for a partner...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, you made that last part up! No way did you taste that!

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: #Well, it looks like I lost fair and square... I guess you'll be taking {NICKNAME} as one of your assistants, then?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But if it takes three chefs, that still leaves one slot remaining... Um... Maybe Paimon and Navia should keep practicing and see how it goes...?

dialogues.speaker: Hilaire
dialogues.text: Uh...Chef Escoffier!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, it's Hilaire! What brings you here?

dialogues.speaker: Hilaire
dialogues.text: ...I heard the news. About the cooking contest — you're doing Gateau Debord, right? I was just wondering if you needed any help?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Huh... And you think you're up to the task, do you?

dialogues.speaker: Hilaire
dialogues.text: Oh... No, I know I'm not there yet. It's actually... my dad who wanted to help.

dialogues.speaker: Escoffier
dialogues.text: Firmin...? Last I heard, you could barely get out of bed...

dialogues.speaker: Firmin
dialogues.text: #Chef Escoffier... Navia, {NICKNAME}... Thank you all so much for everything you're doing for me and my family....

dialogues.speaker: Firmin
dialogues.text: I've had enough of sitting around at home while you run yourselves ragged... If you let me, I'd like to help you win this cooking contest!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Are you sure you're up to the task, Firmin?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Yeah, I was gonna say the same thing...

dialogues.speaker: Firmin
dialogues.text: ...Don't you worry, I'll be fine! ...I'm feeling much better now. I'm sorry, I know I've been rather useless these past few days... but not any more.

dialogues.speaker: Firmin
dialogues.text: ...The fact is, I'm a fine chef, despite recent events. I've proven myself in the Hotel Debord kitchen... So if anyone's qualified to work under Chef Escoffier, it's me! I think... I mean, I hope so...

dialogues.speaker: Escoffier
dialogues.text: Firmin... have you even set foot in a kitchen since leaving Hotel Debord?

dialogues.speaker: Firmin
dialogues.text: I... I have not. But I'm fully rested now! I know I can handle it! ...I'll prove it! Lemme whip something up for you right now!

dialogues.speaker: Firmin
dialogues.text: Huh? That's strange... Why are my hands shaking?

dialogues.speaker: Savanna
dialogues.text: ...What do you call this, Firmin?

dialogues.speaker: Firmin
dialogues.text: I... can't seem to grip my knife...

dialogues.speaker: Savanna
dialogues.text: ...Do it again! ...Again! ...Again!

dialogues.speaker: Savanna
dialogues.text: ...Hopeless. Get out of my kitchen, yesterday!

dialogues.speaker: Firmin
dialogues.text: Ugh...

dialogues.speaker: Hilaire
dialogues.text: Dad! What's wrong?

dialogues.speaker: Firmin
dialogues.text: I don't understand... I was feeling so much better, and then I...

dialogues.speaker: Firmin
dialogues.text: I... Will I... never be able to work in a kitchen again?

dialogues.speaker: Hilaire
dialogues.text: Dad, talk to me! What happened?
...I think the real issue here is not physical exhaustion, but psychological trauma.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Monica? When did you get here?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Even I didn't notice you arrive...

dialogues.speaker: Monica
dialogues.text: Haha... Probably because you were all concentrating so hard on your cooking. I didn't want to interrupt your flow.

dialogues.speaker: Monica
dialogues.text: But anyway... Firmin, I'm so sorry. If only I'd known how serious your situation was, I would've stood up for you sooner!

dialogues.speaker: Firmin
dialogues.text: ...You have nothing to apologize for, Monica. During those long nights of redoing every order, you were the only person who looked out for me.

dialogues.speaker: Monica
dialogues.text: Ah, come on, all I did was make you some tea... I doubt it was much help. Savanna was so ruthless toward you — I probably should've brought you something stronger.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ugh, she sounds like the worst... Alright, another Savanna horror story. Let's hear it!

dialogues.speaker: Monica
dialogues.text: She's been getting harsher and harsher on us ever since she heard about Escoffier's new role in the Fleuve Cendre. Seems like no matter what we make, she'll find something wrong with it...

dialogues.speaker: Savanna
dialogues.text: ...What is this? It looks like a dog's been at it! In the trash, now!

dialogues.speaker: Firmin
dialogues.text: Then, she orders us to redo the dish again and again... but we never know what's going to make her happy.

dialogues.speaker: Savanna
dialogues.text: ...Do it again! ...Do it again! ...Do it again!

dialogues.speaker: Monica
dialogues.text: Every time you remake it, you just get another earful from her...

dialogues.speaker: Savanna
dialogues.text: ...Either straighten yourself out or get out of my kitchen!!!

dialogues.speaker: Firmin
dialogues.text: So now... It seems like just picking up a kitchen utensil gives me flashbacks of her yelling at me...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Aw man... That must be awful.

dialogues.speaker: Firmin
dialogues.text: The more I want to get it perfect, the more my hand shake... And the more scared I am of making another mistake...

dialogues.speaker: Escoffier
dialogues.text: How can you give up so easily, Firmin? You weren't a quitter when you were working for me.

dialogues.speaker: Escoffier
dialogues.text: And even under Savanna, you talk about working late into the night trying to perfect your dishes... that says to me that you still hadn't lost that determination to prove yourself. What changed?

dialogues.speaker: Firmin
dialogues.text: I... I don't know what's come over me. When I think back... I just remember feeling like my heart and my hands were growing heavier and heavier as the shift went on. Each time I had to redo a dish, my heart sank a little further...

dialogues.speaker: Firmin
dialogues.text: Maybe Savanna was right. Maybe I am just hopeless at this...

dialogues.speaker: Hilaire
dialogues.text: Dad...

dialogues.speaker: Escoffier
dialogues.text: I see... Well, it sounds like there are some deep issues at work here. Ones that won't be resolved by merely seeking compensation.

dialogues.speaker: Escoffier
dialogues.text: I will win this contest, and after that, I encourage you to approach Savanna and talk this out.

dialogues.speaker: Firmin
dialogues.text: But, what if you can't find another assistant in time? Clearly, I'm in no state to help out...

dialogues.speaker: Escoffier
dialogues.text: Heh, you think being one person short will ruin my chances? Let's not forget, I taught you and her everything you know!

dialogues.speaker: Escoffier
dialogues.text: Even if I had to go it alone, I would present the perfect gateau!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh... Well, um... Paimon and Navia will still keep practicing, just in case...

dialogues.speaker: Hilaire
dialogues.text: And... and so will I!

dialogues.speaker: Monica
dialogues.text: Um...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah... And if worse comes to worst, we can always get the Spina di Rosula to put out an emergency call for chefs. There's gotta be someone out there, right?

dialogues.speaker: Monica
dialogues.text: Actually, uh... I thought maybe I could help? That's sort of why I'm here...

dialogues.speaker: Escoffier
dialogues.text: Why didn't you say so!?

dialogues.speaker: Monica
dialogues.text: I was going to, but then... Well, this is the first chance I got, heh.

dialogues.speaker: Hilaire
dialogues.text: You'd do this for us? Thank you so much, Monica!

dialogues.speaker: Escoffier
dialogues.text: Alright, fine by me... But aren't you still working for Savanna? Joining the other side seems like a guaranteed way to put your future employment in jeopardy.

dialogues.speaker: Monica
dialogues.text: I know, but it's alright — I've made up my mind. With the way things are, I can't keep working for Savanna much longer anyway. Unless I wanna become the next Firmin...

dialogues.speaker: Firmin
dialogues.text: *sigh*...

dialogues.speaker: Monica
dialogues.text: I'm done with sucking it up. It's time to try and turn things around! If this cooking contest can get Savanna to see the error of her ways... then I'm sure she'll forgive me for this!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I hope you're right...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, Paimon didn't think we'd be poaching from Savanna's staff to get our third person, but there you go... Anyway, Monica's a professional chef, so nothing can possibly go wrong now!

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Great! Then it's settled! And to congratulate you all on making the team... I propose a Spina-sponsored meal to celebrate!

dialogues.speaker: Escoffier
dialogues.text: Spina-sponsored— Wait, you mean I'm cooking?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: #Haha, well, I promised {NICKNAME} a feast in the Fleuve Cendre... And I know how much you've been looking forward to it!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah! Feast, feast, feast!

choices.text: I can help cook.
It'll be good practice for the contest.

dialogues.speaker: Escoffier
dialogues.text: Why, Savanna... Why...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What are you up to?

dialogues.speaker: Escoffier
dialogues.text: Oh... nothing, I was just flicking through the original Codex Debord...

dialogues.speaker: Escoffier
dialogues.text: I... wanted to see if there was anything I'm missing. Something I hadn't noticed before, that might explain why Savanna's so desperate to get her hands on it...

dialogues.speaker: Escoffier
dialogues.text: But I can't find anything. It's just some hastily scribbled recipes in between diary entries from Modeste's adventuring phase... and most of it's not even legible anymore.

dialogues.speaker: Escoffier
dialogues.text: The copy I gave her not only has all the recipes in full, but even includes my own private tips and notes from years of experience... Surely that's infinitely more useful than this old thing?

choices.text: For her, it's probably not about how useful it is...

response.speaker: Escoffier
response.text: Yeah, maybe... Still, it's just hard for me to imagine that the Savanna I knew would go to all this effort just to make a point.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: ...Were you two friends?

response.speaker: Escoffier
response.text: We were... At least, I always thought we were.

response.speaker: Escoffier
response.text: She was a little shy, but meticulous with everything and everyone she dealt with. She made a few mistakes here and there, but she was quick to correct them whenever they were pointed out, and she was always striving to improve as a chef...

response.speaker: Escoffier
response.text: Those qualities are why I recommended her to replace me as head chef... I never imagined for one second that she'd cause Firmin and the other staff so much grief.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: It sounds like you feel... partly responsible?

response.speaker: Escoffier
response.text: ...Ahem! Well, I mean to an extent, of course. I pushed hard for her to get the role.

response.speaker: Escoffier
response.text: And the idea that she turned out like this because of me is... difficult to come to terms with...

response.speaker: Escoffier
response.text: *sigh* I wonder if this is how Modeste felt, back when he was writing the Codex?

choices.text: Speaking of Modeste...

response.speaker: Escoffier
response.text: Yes, with his good friend and co-founder of the Hotel Debord, Savelli.

response.speaker: Escoffier
response.text: The story goes that after Modeste unveiled his Gateau Debord and was hailed as a culinary genius, he was admired and adored by all... But his newfound fame slowly drove him and Savelli apart.

response.speaker: Escoffier
response.text: Unlike Modeste, whose every new creation was an instant hit, Savelli seemed to face setbacks at every turn. Doors that would swing wide open for Modeste would shut in Savelli's face.

response.speaker: Escoffier
response.text: And with Modeste being whisked off to all manner of functions by his celebrity friends, he had less and less time to discuss the culinary arts with Savelli.

response.speaker: Escoffier
response.text: People started gossiping about Savelli, and the relationship between the two gradually soured...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: So what happened to them, ultimately?

response.speaker: Escoffier
response.text: ...Everything came to an abrupt end when Modeste, still in the prime of his life and still hailed as a genius, suddenly died from an acute illness.

response.speaker: Escoffier
response.text: And that was it. They neither had a decisive split, nor got the chance to properly reconcile. Their story just... came to an end.

response.speaker: Escoffier
response.text: One rumor had it that Savelli actually killed Modeste out of jealousy, even as the latter was hoping to make amends...

response.speaker: Escoffier
response.text: Unlikely — it's a popular theory, but there's no real basis for it. At least, there are no records of Savelli ever being convicted of a crime.

response.speaker: Escoffier
response.text: Still, beyond a point, there's no way of knowing what truly happened in the past... All we can do is try to make sure the present doesn't go quite as badly.

response.speaker: Escoffier
response.text: And that's why I have to win this contest tomorrow! Then get the truth about everything that's been going on, even if it means cracking her open like a nut!

choices.text: With me on the team, there's no way we can lose.

response.speaker: Escoffier
response.text: Really? Well, I like the confidence. Don't let me down tomorrow, then. You'd better bring your A game.

choices.text: With you on the team, there's no way we can lose.

response.speaker: Escoffier
response.text: Hehe, you're right about that! Just follow my lead, and victory will be ours!

choices.text: Is it true?
Didn't he have a falling-out with someone as well?
...And more an issue of head chef's pride.

dialogues.speaker: Escoffier
dialogues.text: How's it going? Have you picked a dish yet? Choose wisely — I expect you to present <color=#00E1FFFF>the most delicious thing</color> on the menu.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: #Ahhh... I wish I could eat that all over again... It's not often that Escoffier goes all-out like this, and it's all because of you, {NICKNAME}!

dialogues.speaker: Hilaire
dialogues.text: Wow... I don't know if I'll ever be able to cook as good as that...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Is that Navia over there? It's been a while, let's go say hi!

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Escoffier? Could this mean...? Hmm...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? You know that name, Navia?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Yeah... Let's stick to the plan and go back to the Fleuve Cendre for now. That's where we'll find Escoffier anyway.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon doesn't see Monica and Savanna anywhere... Guess they went back to the kitchen?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: We'll only complicate things even more if we go looking for them now. Let's head to the Fleuve Cendre.

dialogues.speaker: Customers in Spirited Discussion
dialogues.text: Wait, she looks like... Is that Escoffier?

dialogues.speaker: Customers in Spirited Discussion
dialogues.text: Escoffier's back? Yes! I've missed her cooking!

dialogues.speaker: Customers in Spirited Discussion
dialogues.text: I was just saying, Hotel Debord is nothing without her...

dialogues.speaker: Customers in Spirited Discussion
dialogues.text: You can't match Escoffier's talent!

dialogues.speaker: Monica
dialogues.text: I'm sorry, I'm so sorry!

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: ...Escoffier, are you sure this is a good idea? You accepted her terms a little hastily...

dialogues.speaker: Escoffier
dialogues.text: Oh, it'll be fine. Let's head back to the Fleuve Cendre so I can get prepping.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: I've always called it "chopping stuff up," not "mise en place"... But it's basically the same thing, right?

dialogues.speaker: Escoffier
dialogues.text: Oh, Navia... The difference in your case is that "mise en place" is chopping stuff up WITHOUT sending juices flying all over the kitchen!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Custom-made equipment from the Fontaine Research Institute, huh... That's some pretty hi-tech food prep. Paimon's never used anything this weird before— Uh, cool! Not weird!

dialogues.speaker: Escoffier
dialogues.text: Slowly... and carefully... Not a drop too much, and not a drop too little...

dialogues.speaker: Escoffier
dialogues.text: Ahem... that didn't count! I was... experimenting!

dialogues.speaker: Escoffier
dialogues.text: (Get with it, Escoffier! Everyone's watching...)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Phew... That was a dream come true... Paimon never knew Fontainian cuisine could be this good...
